WHAT IMPERFECT EXPERIMENTS CAN ACQUIRE FOR RELIABLE LATER COMPUTATION
Astra foundational learning/computation branch — 31 October 2026

STATUS AND SCIENTIFIC OBJECT

The completed central construction is a reusable solver that learns through
certified requests. It has a finite lifetime budget of failed checks under
bounded, potentially biased and query-dependent action error. The budget is
controlled by a resolution-dependent spectral comparison quantity, not exact
algebra dimension. Generic full-rank perturbations can leave that quantity small.

A matching investigation of information access shows why this change of object
matters: preparing an accurate source-free service for every future right-hand
side can require exponentially many fixed-accuracy experiments, even for sources
with condition number two and generated algebra dimension two. The later task
itself can reveal a useful probe. Buying better measurement accuracy instead has
an explicit dimension-dependent calibration price in a specified cost model.

The ingredients of the positive learner are established: online operator learning,
least-change/halfspace corrections, spectral projection, low-rank matrix updates,
and residual validation. Dunagan--Harvey already amortize acquired preconditioners
over related solves. The proposed research addition is the combined noisy access,
approximate-comparator, all-request service theorem and the contrasting information
boundary. Historical priority for this combination and practical superiority are
not established. This is not a claimed general theory of intelligence.

The previous exact algebra compiler is accepted at its earned scope. This work
does not re-audit it or assume its robustness. No exact block structure is used
by the construction below. The auxiliary spectral-envelope construction provides
a different, explicitly costed offline capability under stronger resolution.

1. SOURCE, NOISE AND TASK CONTRACT

There are k fixed Hermitian operators A_j on C^N and known scalar bounds

  0 < mu I <= A_j <= L I.                                  (1.1)

The bounds are input conditions, not conclusions inferred from finitely many
noisy actions. They give coercivity, not a useful basis or solver. A common way
to meet this contract is a known regularization floor added to bounded positive
operators; its physical availability and cost are application premises.

INDEPENDENT AUDIT OF THE DEMAND-REVEALED COMPUTATION THEOREM
31 October 2026 — operational_learning collaborator

VERDICT

No material flaw found in the exact-arithmetic theorem. The noisy mixture
interface, sound halfspace, approximate-comparator decrease, solution certificate,
spectral comparison quantity, and scalar-plus-low-rank implementation agree.
The finite-precision extension needed an explicit acceptance/correction guard
band; that issue was reported and the root's revised section 9 repairs it.
The numerical implementation remains empirical, not outward-rounded validation.
No historical-priority or practical-superiority conclusion follows from this audit.

MATHEMATICAL CHECKS

1. Convex weights preserve the per-action norm error eta. Projecting away the
   imaginary parallel component is real-orthogonal projection onto a space
   containing the true Hermitian action and cannot increase that error.
2. With v*r real, ||sym(rv*)||_F^2=(||r||^2+(v*r)^2)/2. The lower bound on this
   denominator and the earned halfspace h=a(a-eta) are correct.
3. Against every fixed C within operator distance zeta, expanding the squared
   product-Frobenius distance and then clipping gives the stated decrease
   (a-eta)(a-eta-2zeta)/||theta||_2^2. The comparator is analysis-only; no advice
   or unmeasured subspace is used. Telescoping gives the lifetime bound.
4. The accepted-candidate certificate bounds RELATIVE SOLUTION ERROR by
   (a+eta)/(mu-a-eta), not merely relative residual. This derivation is sound.
5. E_zeta is exactly the minimum comparison energy: Weyl bounds eigenvalue
   displacement, and moving eigenvalues toward each alpha_j attains the bound.
6. Updates have support in span{v,r}; clipping leaves alpha_j unchanged on the
   orthogonal complement. The common retained span and the explicit reduced

RESULTS AND USEFUL FAILURES
Astra foundational learning/computation — 31 October 2026

1. CONTROLLED COMPARISON: SAME TASKS, SOURCE, NOISE AND TOLERANCE

N=192; k=3; 120 fixed tasks. Sources have a shared rank-five core with
different noncommuting, mixed-spectrum actions, plus generic independent
diagonal tails of operator norm <=.002. The learner sees neither the core
nor its basis. Source error <=.003; acceptance threshold .060; known
spectral interval [.85,2.6]. Scalar initialization is (1,1.1,.9).

The fixed continuous nonlinear oracle masks part of the core response.
Every method sees that same callback on identical requested (theta,b) pairs.
All individual action observations already paid for are available equally
to the individual halfspace, PSB and BFGS methods.

Method                          Original actions  Failed checks  Retained dim
Aggregate halfspace                         582             74           131
Aggregate halfspace +2 mixed probes          504             16            32
Individual halfspace                        468             36           130
Individual halfspace +2 single probes        420             12            50
Ordinary individual PSB                      465             35           120
Ordinary PSB +2 single probes                415             11            45
Ordinary individual BFGS                     453             31           109
Ordinary BFGS +2 single probes               420             12            48
Fresh checked CG                           1248            113             0

Every row returned all 120 answers. Maximum true relative solution errors
ranged .0388--.0547; maximum reported certificates ranged .0772--.0798.
The theorem certifies the output from the fresh defect, not from a recursive
CG residual or a claimed recovered rank. Source counts include validation,
failed attempts and directed probes. Different methods stop at the same
certificate threshold, not at exactly equal true errors.

The ordinary PSB variant slightly wins. It also has a proved noisy lifetime
bound; the main halfspace bound permits a wider provable noise margin.
BFGS sometimes increases the selected Frobenius potential (downward progress
as low as -.0522), so that proof cannot be transferred to BFGS by analogy.
